name: cloud-code
description: Cloud Code — our own signed build of Acode (the Android code editor), vendored at ac_cloud-code/ as owned code (#562), with a 7-tab bottom nav over it: Backlog | Editor | Repos | Home | Agents | Browser | MyTerminal. Acode is the UPSTREAM PROJECT, never the product name. The Editor tab is Acode untouched; the other six live in src/cloud/ behind one seam in src/main.js. See CLOUD-CODE.md.
_doc_vendored_engine: Byte-identical to ac_cloud-code/build.sh, enforced by cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh parity check so the shipped engine and the vendored copy cannot drift.
_doc_name: #562 asked for ac_cloud-ide-acode. Not used: #561 retired the cloud-ide brand, and test-app-names-pattern.sh T9 fails any build.json value matching cloud[-_ ]?ide as a whole word, which 'cloud-ide-acode' does. cloud-code is canonical cloud-{name} (#351), collides with no fleet id, and names the function, not the upstream.

android._doc_application_id: The install identity, set by build-extras.gradle in onVariants. Cordova's widget id (config.xml) stays com.foxdebug.acode because it is also the Java namespace that upstream plugin sources import R from; only the applicationId moves. A new id, so it installs NEXT TO an upstream Acode rather than over it (and the one provider authority upstream hardcoded is now ${applicationId}-scoped for the same reason).
android._doc_version: version_name follows Acode's own package.json version at the pinned revision. version_code starts at 1 and must be bumped for the fleet updater to offer a rebuild (it only offers strictly newer codes).
android._doc_target_sdk: Not ours to set: Acode's hooks/post-process.js pins targetSdk 28 for the F-Droid flavour (legacy storage + exec), which is the flavour built here. Recorded so the number is visible, not restated in gradle.
android._doc_no_gradle_module: No gradle_module is declared on purpose. The Android project is generated by `cordova platform add android` at build time (platforms/, gitignored), so there is no committed build.gradle, and T6 fails a declared module with none. The launcher label is written into config.xml <name> from .name by the engine instead.

upstream._doc: Full clone vendored as owned code (#253/#469: a clone, not a fork — no .git, no upstream remote, the submodule inlined). The brief said 'Acode is GPL — verify': it is NOT. license.txt at the pinned revision is MIT (Foxdebug / Ajit Kumar). The GPL in upstream's tree is the PREBUILT proot/talloc binaries and Alpine rootfs of src/plugins/proot, which are PRUNED here: they are GPL-2.0/LGPL binaries shipped without corresponding source, and the F-Droid flavour this fleet builds removes that plugin anyway. Full inventory in CLOUD-CODE.md; guarded by test/test-licence-clean.sh.

flavor._doc: Upstream's own build axes (utils/scripts/build.sh): 'paid' = no AdMob plugin and no ads; 'fdroid' = no proot plugin and no Google Play Billing (cordova-plugin-iap). The engine reproduces exactly those two choices; nothing in the editor is patched to get there.

artifact_assert._doc: Read by cloud-code-engine.sh::_assert_apk_payload. gradle signs a perfectly valid APK around an empty www/, so the BUILT ARTIFACT must carry the web bundle AND this app's own layer: the nav module's marker string is looked for inside the shipped main.js, so an APK built from a tree that lost the seam fails here, not on the phone.

tests._doc: Shell testers under ac_cloud-code/test/, run by cloud-android-test-engine.sh shell in the ship workflow's FIRST step, before any toolchain. None needs a build.

cordova_surface._doc: Read by test/test-cordova-plugin-surface.sh — the Cordova form of #543's Capacitor trap. web_roots are walked to DERIVE every service name the bundle hands the bridge (cordova.exec(ok, err, 'Service', ...)); the registration side is DERIVED from package.json::cordova.plugins (what `cordova prepare` installs) minus upstream.flavor.removed_plugins, each mapped through package.json's file: dependency to its plugin.xml <feature name>. No service name is written in the tester.
